payload.headline: Meta dips 1.2% to 618.87, resting on support; cash flow still lags price

summary.thesis: Sales are growing fast, but costs have grown faster. Free cash flow has dropped to 28.6B from 44.8B, so 618.87 already prices in a recovery the data does not show yet.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a lower price or for the 2027-01-27 report. Swing: wait, because the price is caught between a support zone just below and a resistance zone just above.
summary.act_at: buy at 475.85; trim above 707.21; swing only on a hold of 605.33–611.95 or a close above 648.45

payload.happening: Meta closed at 618.87, down 1.2% on the day. The stock is in a downtrend and trades below its 20-day average of 629.34, its 50-day average of 680.02 and its 200-day average of 629.15. Today's news was about products: Meta reportedly launched or is testing Direct, a stand-alone messaging app for Instagram, and reportedly added a tool that helps creators fight copycat and AI-modified reposts. The next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
payload.business: Demand is still strong. Revenue grew 27.53% over the last twelve months to 241.6B, and the gross margin is 81.03%. Growth is slowing, though: sales grew 26.07% from a year earlier in the latest quarter, down from 33.08% two quarters ago. The bigger change is in profits and cash. The operating margin (profit from the core business per dollar of sales) fell to 32.86% from 43.23%. Free cash flow (cash left after running the business and paying for investment) fell to 28.6B from 44.8B, which is a margin of only 11.86%. R&D spending equals 31.68% of revenue. The company now has more debt than cash (net cash -1.2B, with 83.7B of debt), and its filings flag a 29% miss against forecasts last quarter. These are the facts that matter for the business. Some things only affect mood or governance: the Direct app and the creator tools have no figures behind them yet, and insiders reportedly sold $14.2M outside their pre-set plans. At risk: how fast cash flow comes back from heavy spending.

worth.text: The methods disagree because they start from different cash figures. The DCF (a value built from future free cash flow) starts from today's weak 28.6B. It gives 243.13 in the bear case, 368.76 in the base case and 500.51 in the bull case, and all three are below 618.87. To justify today's price, free cash flow would need to start growing at 38.2% a year. That is higher than every growth figure in the data: 28% sales growth last year, 24% over three years and 17% expected EPS growth. Even at 30% starting growth the DCF gives only 459.62. Methods based on sales look kinder. The price is 6.6 times sales, near the peer median of 6.2. After adjusting for growth it is about level with peers (1.02), and it sits at the 38th percentile of Meta's own five-year range, which puts the own-history value at 475.85 to 707.21. Earnings look modest at a trailing P/E (price divided by profit per share) of 21.2. My range runs from the low end of Meta's own history to its midpoint. The price is inside that range only if margins recover. If the operating margin fell to 24%, the DCF value would drop to 236.05.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow recovers toward the earlier 44.8B as the spending pays off, instead of staying near 28.6B.

bull: Sales are still growing 27.53% a year, with an 81.03% gross margin, so demand is not the problem.
The price-to-sales ratio of 6.6 is at only the 38th percentile of Meta's own five-year history, and after adjusting for growth it is in line with peers (1.02).
The midpoint of Meta's own history is 707.21, and the busiest call option strike is 700 with 33264 contracts open, so there is room upward if margins recover.
bear: Free cash flow fell to 28.6B from 44.8B, and the operating margin fell to 32.86% from 43.23%.
The price implies 38.2% yearly growth in free cash flow, but the highest growth figure in the data is 28%, and the bull DCF is only 500.51.
Quarterly sales growth slowed to 26.07% from 33.08%, and the company missed forecasts by 29% last quarter.

levels.what: Bottom of the nearer support zone (605.33–611.95), just under today's price. A close below it opens the stronger zone at 591.53–598.97, which has 6 touches.
Low end of Meta's own price-to-sales history and close to the 459.62 DCF value at 30% growth. Buying at this level does not depend on a full margin recovery.
Midpoint of Meta's own history. Above it the price treats the cash-flow recovery as already done, so trimming would be the action there.

longterm.why: The business is graded C, the committee call is Reduce, and 618.87 is above every DCF value. Buying here pays in advance for a cash-flow recovery that has not happened yet.

swing.why: The price is in a downtrend and sits between support at 605.33–611.95 and resistance starting at 622.66. That resistance is less than one typical daily move (ATR 22.07) away, so a trade has too little upside for its stop. Enter only on a hold of 605.33–611.95 or on a close above 648.45.

decision.timing: Options price a 10.1% move by Dec 18 and a 13.1% move by Jan 15, both before the 2027-01-27 report. That report on margins and cash flow is the deciding event, so no long-term entry before it unless the price reaches 475.85 first.

change_mind: The 2027-01-27 report shows the operating margin moving back toward 43.23% and trailing free cash flow rising above 28.6B. That would support the high end of 707.21 and turn wait into buy on a pullback to 605.33.
A close below 591.53, the bottom of the 6-touch support zone, would deepen the downtrend and point toward 475.85 as the next buy level.
A close above 648.45 would clear both resistance zones and break the pattern of lower highs. That would turn the swing call into enter, with a stop at 605.33.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait. The price fell to 618.87 from 626.41 and remains above every DCF value (the top is 500.51), which confirms the price is ahead of the cash flow.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
